newsitem.title: JORDAN: Amman stocks drop for third consecutive day.
newsitem.headline: Amman stocks drop for third consecutive day.

text.p: Jordan's stock market ended on Wednesday with a third consecutive fall after global fund buying petered out, dealers said. The official 60-share Amman Financial Market (AFM) index shed 0.48 percent to close at 160.34 points in moderate turnover of1.3 million dinars ($1.8 million).
The market has faltered since Sunday, when a two-week long buying spree by global funds focused primarily on two mining blue-chip stocks and cement fizzled out.
"Prices were naturally expected to see a correction after supply became much more than demand," said broker Ibrahim Odeh of Wataniyeh Financial Services.
The retreat by foreign funds has erased some of the gains which sent market prices to their highest levels in nearly two years.

Trade was again dominated by Jordan Cement, which spearheaded the market bull run, accounting for nearly half of Wednesday's daily volume. It shed 0.08 dinars to close at 4.10 dinars in moderate trade worth 638,431 dinars.
In the absence of substantial emerging fund purchases, local institutional buyers appear to be firmly focused on blue chips.
Majority state owned Jordan Phosphate Mines fell 0.08 dinars to 3.90 dinars in the second busiest activity worth 137,844 dinars.
The third busiest stock, Jordan National Bank fell 0.09 dinars to 2.06 dinars in 93,182 dinars worth of trade.
Overall falling shares outnumbered gainers by 32 to six while another nine traded but closed unchanged.
The private Pearl Index of the 45 best-performing shares in terms of turnover and financial performance shed 0.24 percent to 80.93 points, 2.96 percent down from the start of the year.
